ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 6516, as amended), its Enforcement Decree (as amended), the Prohibition of Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation of Weapons of Mass Destruction Act (Act No. 13884, as amended), the Commercial Act (Act No. 1000, as amended), and the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act (Act No. 6330, as amended), together with the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit's regulatory guidance requiring legal-person customer due diligence and beneficial ownership verification for all corporate clients.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (company registration certificate issued by the competent court registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court of Korea Registry Office (Court of Registration at the registered office in Seoul)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: Registry extract authenticated by the Supreme Court Registry and then embossed with an Apostille certificate by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea for use only in Apostille Convention member states. Consular Legalization route for non-member states: registry attestation -> Ministry of Foreign Affairs legalization division -> consular legalization at the embassy or consulate of the destination state in Seoul. The two routes are mutually exclusive; they must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Korean corporate registry extract showing absence of liquidation, bankruptcy or dissolution entries)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court of Korea Registry Office (issuing through the IROS portal or the local commercial registry of the registered office)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: certified true copy issued by the registry, followed by an Apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea; valid only in Apostille states. Consular Legalization route: certified copy -> Ministry of Foreign Affairs verification -> legalization by the destination country's consular post in Seoul; never add apostille or consular legalization sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and signed Power of Attorney (authorizing the incorporation counsel and opening of bank accounts)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company's board of directors (initial manager or director of the future Yuhan Hoesa) in the presence of a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: notarization by the Korean notary, then Apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) for member states. Consular Legalization route: notarization -> MOFA legalization certificate -> consular legalization by the destination state embassy or consulate in Korea. Parallel alternatives only; do not chain.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Copy of the Articles of Association (Yuhan Hoesa bylaws)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean notary public and/or the Supreme Court Registry Office (registered copy)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: notarial or registry certified copy -> Apostille certificate from MOFA. Consular Legalization route: certified copy -> MOFA legalization -> destination state consular legalization in Seoul. The route is selected exclusively by the destination state's membership in the Apostille Convention; no sequential cross-use.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter (bank confirmation of domestic or foreign bank account conduct, signatory authority and no adverse status)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean commercial bank or international bank's Korean branch (issuing under banking secrecy using the bank's headed paper)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: bank officer's signature authenticated by a Korean notary public -> Apostille by MOFA for use in member states. Consular Legalization route: notarized bank letter -> MOFA authentication -> consular legalization at the destination state's embassy or consulate in Korea. Use only the route applicable to the receiving country; never combine routes.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All directors, shareholders with 25% or more direct or indirect ownership, ultimate beneficial owners, authorized signatories and bank signatories must be screened before incorporation against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, EU/UK consolidated sanctions, and the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit's asset-freezing designations under the Prohibition of Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation of Weapons of Mass Destruction Act. Screening must be independently verified against at least two commercial AML databases, including PEP and adverse media tiers, with full-name, alias and passport-level matching; every potential match must be dispositioned in writing in a signed compliance memorandum, and ongoing screening is required until all bank accounts are opened and active, with repeat screening every 90 days.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Internet Registration Office of the Supreme Court of Korea ('IROS') online commercial registry and name availability search module (operated by the Registry Office of the Supreme Court of Korea)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Korean trade names must be expressed in a language that can be recorded by the Korean commercial registry; foreign shareholders are required to provide a phonetic transliteration into Korean script, and the registry registers the Korean-script transliteration as the primary name while the Latin-script name is reflected only as a transliterated alias. The four-tier naming protocol requires: (1) a distinctive distinguishing element, (2) a descriptive business purpose clause, (3) the registered trade name of the enterprise, and (4) the statutory corporate form suffix indicating limited liability. Hanja ideographs may be used only where expressly permitted by the registry and never alter the Korean phonetic reading or create identity with a pre-existing name.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of South Korea (상법), Act No. 1000, promulgated January 27, 1962, as completely amended by Act No. 17758, December 23, 2020; specifically Articles 169 (Juridical Person), 253 (Incorporation by Promoters), 287 (Articles of Incorporation), 288-292 (Incorporation Procedures), 295 (Subscription for Shares and Payment), 312 (Incorporation of Share Company), 316 (Procedures for Establishment of Corporation), 318 (Registration of Incorporation), 386 (Qualification of Directors), 388 (Remuneration of Directors), 393 (Resolution of Board of Directors), 398 (Contracts between the Corporation and Directors), and Article 55-2 of the Framework Act on Commercial Registration (상업등기법).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Korean Commercial Registration Network (등기정보센터) operated by the Supreme Court of Korea; physical filing counter at the Commercial Registry Division (상업등기과) of the District Court (지방법원) having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office address; electronic filing portal: IROS (인터넷등기소) at https://www.iros.go.kr
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation Application (주식회사설립등기신청서) for a limited liability company (유한회사), together with the Articles of Incorporation (정관) and the Promoters' Minutes of the Incorporation Meeting (발기인총회의사록)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Under Article 287 of the Commercial Act, there is no statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company). The capital amount stated in the Articles of Incorporation must be fully paid-in to the domestic bank escrow (designated deposit) account before the incorporation registration. Korean regulations require the paid-in amount to be deposited in a Korean commercial bank (e.g., Hana Bank, Kookmin Bank, Shinhan Bank) in the name of the company or its promoter, with a balance certificate (잔액증명서) issued for the court filing. Non-resident promoters may open the escrow account through a duly appointed proxy holder or with an Alien Registration Card, and the funds must remain blocked until the court completes the incorporation registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Digital Certificate and Verify Registered Office Address with Local Municipality
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Respective District Court, Municipal (Eup/Myeon/Dong) Community Center, and authorized certificate authorities for accredited digital signatures (e.g., KICA, SignKorea, or the Supreme Court's IROS-issued administrative digital certificate)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The designated promoter or its authorized representative in Korea must first obtain a Korean accredited digital certificate (공인인증서) from a licensed certificate authority to access IROS. In parallel, verify that the proposed registered office address is a physical, rentable premise and not a virtual office in order to qualify for commercial registration; the landlord must provide a certified copy of the real estate register (등기사항전부증명서) and a copy of the lease agreement. For non-resident entities, engage a local resident agent with a power of attorney (위임장), notarized in the country of execution and legalized with a consular apostille, to act as the applicant. Confirm that the street address is correctly reflected in the municipal address system, and obtain a building owner's consent letter for the registered office if the lease is not yet fully executed. Submit the digital certificate, address documents, and lease draft to the formation attorney for pre-review.
required_dossiers: Power of Attorney (notarized and apostilled/legalized) for the local resident agent
Copy of the promoter's passport or foreign corporation's certificate of incorporation (translated into Korean)
Lease agreement or building owner's consent letter for the registered office address
Certified copy of real estate register (등기사항전부증명서) of the office premises
Korean accredited digital certificate (공인인증서) details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality or registry flags the address as non-compliant or an e-address mismatch, immediately obtain a revised lease with a corrected address notation from the landlord and file a correction notice with the municipal community center; any delay of more than 5 business days may be cured by switching to an alternative physically verifiable address and submitting an updated lease with a new owner consent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft, Notarize, and File the Articles of Incorporation (정관) and Capital Escrow Establishment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Accredited Notary Public (공증인) in Korea and the Korea Money & Securities Wire (escrow bank); subsequently the District Court Commercial Registry via IROS
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The formation attorney drafts the Articles of Incorporation in Korean, incorporating mandatory clauses under Article 287 such as the corporate name, objectives (which must precisely reflect the ISIC 6201 and 511210 business scope: software development, cloud infrastructure, database publishing, API and DevOps tools), the address of the registered office, the total authorised capital amount, the number of units (지분) to be issued, the method of public notice, and the names of the promoters. The Articles must be notarized by a Korean notary public, and the notary will verify the identity of the promoters or their proxies. After notarization, the capital must be paid into a domestic bank escrow account (가설계좌) under the name of the company or the promoter; the bank will issue a balance certificate (잔액증명서) confirming payment. The promoter then files the notarized Articles together with a request for capital deposit release (금전신탁계약해지) via IROS or in-person at the court; the court examines compliance, and upon approval issues the Certificate of Incorporation Registration (설립등기완료). The escrow is released to the company operating account upon completion of registration.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation (정관)
Promoter identification documents (passport or corporate registration)
Certificate of capital deposit (잔액증명서) from the escrow bank
Promoters' written consent to the Articles (if executed by proxy, the notarized power of attorney)
If a foreign investor: Foreign Investment Notification/report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (외국인투자촉진법) if any foreign investment exceeds KRW 100 million
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a correction order (보정명령) regarding omissions in the Articles, such as an overly broad objective clause, submit a revised Korean translation and a formal supplementary statement (보정서) through IROS within 14 days. If the capital deposit certificate is deemed stale (issued >30 days), obtain a refreshed certificate from the bank. If the foreign investment report is missing or rejected, file a corrective amendment with the KOTRA Investment Ombudsman or the relevant Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy window, and resubmit the registration after receiving the corrected filing receipt.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Corporate Registration with the Commercial Registry and Apply for Business Registration Certificate (사업자등록증)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registry Division of the District Court (via IROS) for incorporation; thereafter the local District Tax Office (세무서) under the National Tax Service (국세청) for business registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the court accepts the incorporation filing and issues the official registration number and the corporate registration certificate, the company must apply for a business registration certificate within 20 days of the registration date under the Value-Added Tax Act. Submit the incorporation certificate, the articles of incorporation, the registered seal certificate (인감증명서), the certificate of capital paid-in, lease agreement for the registered office, and a copy of the CEO's identification to the local district tax office having jurisdiction over the registered address. For a Yuhan Hoesa (LLC), the tax registration is processed as a corporate taxpayer (법인) and the company will receive a business registration number (사업자등록번호) which is also the VAT registration number. The application may be completed online through the Home Tax Service (홈택스) or in person. Upon approval, the company must obtain a corporate seal certificate (법인인감증명서) from the district court, which is a prerequisite for opening bank accounts and executing contracts.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation registration (등기사항전부증명서)
Certified copy of the Articles of Incorporation (정관 사본)
Registered seal certificate (인감증명서) and corporate seal (법인인감)
Lease agreement for the registered office
Balance certificate or bank statement evidencing paid-in capital
Passport/ID of the Chief Executive Officer
Power of attorney if filing by a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the district tax office sends a message requiring supplementary documents (보완요구), respond within 10 days by submitting the missing items via HTS. If the CEO is a non-resident without an Alien Registration Card, the tax office may demand an additional proof of a local tax representative (납세관리인); promptly appoint a tax representative with a power of attorney on form < 국세기본법 > and submit the appointment notice through the National Tax Service.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Corporate Bank Accounts, Register for VAT and E-Procurement, and Execute Banking Agreements with Stripe and Mercury ACH
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Bank branch where the company will maintain accounts (e.g., Hana Bank, Kookmin Bank, Shinhan Bank); National Tax Service (홈택스) for VAT registration; Financial Services Commission (금융위원회) indirectly for e-banking and AML compliance; Stripe and Mercury ACH as international payment processors requiring corporate KYC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The CEO or authorized directorial signatories must appear in person or with a notarized power of attorney at the chosen commercial bank to open a corporate operating account (법인통장) in the name of Yuhan Hoesa. Provide the business registration certificate, the corporate seal certificate, a copy of the Articles of Incorporation, and the identification of all authorized signatories. The bank will conduct customer due diligence (CDD) and enhanced due diligence for any non-resident signatory; all accounts must be categorized as 'corporate account' to enable export-import settlement and online payments. Concurrently, log into Home Tax Service (홈택스) and complete the VAT registration if not already done via the business registration certificate: the company will file VAT quarterly (January and July) under the general VAT scheme. For the target payment rails, register a Stripe Korea or Stripe global account using the company's legal name, business registration number, and bank account details; for Mercury ACH, complete the online application with the company's formation documents and a board resolution authorizing banking access. Upon approval, set up the payment gateway and accounting integration. Finally, register for the Korean government e-procurement system (나라장터) only if the company intends to bid for public contracts; otherwise this step is optional.
required_dossiers: Business registration certificate (사업자등록증)
Corporate seal certificate (법인인감증명서) and corporate seal
Certificate of incorporation registration (등기사항전부증명서)
Idential documents (passport or national ID) of all authorized signatories
Board resolution authorizing account opening (if the pro-forma resolution is not used, adopt a dedicated resolution)
Registered office lease agreement
For non-resident signatories: Alien Registration Card or notarized power of attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank or payment processor rejects the application due to incomplete KYC (commonly lacking a physical office visit or a clear source of funds), request a written deficiency notice and cure within the stated grace period. For Stripe or Mercury, if the upload of the Korean business certification documents fails due to translation or apostille requirements, use a Korean court-issued English abstract (등기사항증명서 영문) and a sworn translation from a licensed Korean translator; if the payment processor still requires a physical US presence, formally lease a US registered agent service and register the company as a foreign business in the relevant US state only if necessary, but such step is outside the Korean statutory formation flow and should be avoided unless the payment rail demands it.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable (pure digital service and software publishing under ISIC 6201; NAICS 511210)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt (no physical manufacturing, chemical process, assembly, warehousing, or stationary emission sources; the company operates a cloud-based DevOps and API monitoring platform with no on-site industrial activity)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable (no wastewater discharge, VOC emissions, hazardous waste treatment, or stack emissions; only office-generated municipal solid waste and standard e-waste recycling obligations under the Act on the Promotion of Saving and Recycling of Resources apply)

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable (no fire permit under the Act on the Installation, Maintenance, and Safety Control of Fire-Fighting Systems is required because the registered office is a standard commercial office not classified as a high-risk occupancy; however, the company remains subject to general workplace safety obligations under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, such as office fire extinguisher compliance and emergency evacuation signage, enforced by the Ministry of Employment and Labor, but no pre-operational civil defense approval is required)

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online portal: HomeTax (www.hometax.go.kr). Export customs clearance is administered by the Korea Customs Service (KCS) through UniPass (www.unipass.customs.go.kr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Korean Yuhan Hoesa LLC, the tax registration procedure is: (1) incorporate with the Korean corporate registry; (2) commence the business and within 20 days file the Business Registration application with the competent district tax office via HomeTax, using the statutory electronic form, digital certificate, and the Korean tax agent's credentials; (3) attach the certificate of incorporation, articles of association, foreign-equity ownership registry, business license, and lease document; (4) after verification, the NTS issues a 10-digit Business Registration Number, which functions as both corporate TIN and VAT registration number; (5) register the entity in the e-tax invoice system and the KCS exporter identification in UniPass; and (6) open a Korean won corporate bank account and a foreign-currency account for export and offshore service proceeds. For a foreign non-resident entity that itself engages in Korean taxable supply without a Korean branch, the NTS requires registration of that foreign entity and application for a foreign business registration number via a duly authorized tax agent; the agent identifies a resident place of business or, if none exists, designates a tax representative pursuant to the Framework Act on National Taxes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korean tax law does not contain a check-the-box election. A Yuhan Hoesa is definitively taxed at entity level under the Corporate Income Tax Act. No hybrid mismatch election is available; adjustments prescribed by the Act for International Tax Coordination are compulsory and not elective.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No mandatory turnover threshold in KRW for corporate VAT registration. Any person carrying on a taxable business in South Korea must register with the NTS within 20 days of business commencement. For a Yuhan Hoesa LLC, VAT registration is automatic through Business Registration. The KRW 80 million simplified taxpayer threshold does not apply to capital companies; it is reserved for certain individual entrepreneurs.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Korea operates a real-time electronic tax invoice (e-tax invoice) reporting regime through the NTS HomeTax system. Corporate taxpayers are required to issue e-tax invoices and transmit the e-tax invoice data to the NTS via HomeTax open API, EDI/SFTP, or accredited ASP providers. Transmission is due the day after issuance. The NTS does not grant a pre-issuance authorization or physical fiscal stamp; anti-fraud integrity is maintained through mandatory digital-certificate authentication of the issuer, NTS-assigned e-tax invoice unique numbers, and automatic cross-matching of transmitted invoices to the VAT return and periodic tax invoice statements. Any invoice not reported to the NTS before the VAT filing deadline exposes the taxpayer to statutory surcharges, non-declaration penalties, or reduction or denial of input VAT deduction.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For a Korean Yuhan Hoesa LLC, the 0% VAT rate applies to (i) goods exported from South Korea, where export declaration and actual departure are evidenced, and (ii) qualifying services supplied to non-residents, paid in foreign currency, and actually performed, used, or consumed outside Korea, including database, API monitoring, and other developer infrastructure cloud services. The supply must be documented by a zero-rate tax invoice issued under the VAT Act. Payment must be received into a Korean bank account, observable in the foreign exchange records, within the statutory export-proceeds period.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) / Export Clearance Certificate issued by the Korea Customs Service through UniPass.
Bill of Lading (or Air Waybill) naming the foreign buyer or consignee and evidencing departure of goods from a Korean port or airport.
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) / Foreign Exchange Bank Receipt proving repatriation and settlement of export proceeds in Korea.
Commercial invoice, export contract, and Foreign Exchange Transactions Act documentation supporting the link between the foreign customer's payment and the zero-rated supply.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS audits cross-check the Customs Export Declaration, foreign exchange remittance data, and e-tax invoice records. Absent a complete documentation bundle, the export is recharacterized as a domestic supply, causing 10% VAT to be assessed at the export invoice value plus surcharges under the Framework Act on National Taxes and statutory interest. Intentional fraudulent export claims can attract criminal liability under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act and extend the tax reassessment period from 5 years to up to 10 years. Refunded input VAT is clawed back with interest if the export zero-rating is disallowed.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) together with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) and licensed foreign exchange banks under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a liberalised but regulated foreign exchange regime under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The Korean won is convertible on the current account for trade and service payments, subject to submission of underlying documentation and prior bank screening. Capital account transactions, including inbound equity investment and inbound or outbound loans, require a foreign exchange declaration or a certificate of notification to a designated FX bank; conversion of KRW to foreign currency for capital purposes requires evidence of the authorised transaction. There is no mandatory surrender requirement for export proceeds, but exporters are subject to statutory settlement-period limits. Profit remittances by foreign-invested companies are permitted under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, provided the company files tax returns in Korea and demonstrates that the earnings have been legitimately generated and taxed; withholding tax at the applicable treaty rate is deducted at source. Dividend remittances require evidence of foreign investment registration, a board resolution declaring dividends, and audited financial statements. In practice, banks apply strict transaction-purpose reviews, and any attempt to convert KRW for speculative use or without an underlying trade or investment event is rejected. The effectiveness of the system is high, with the Bank of Korea acting as the central repository of FX data and the Ministry of Economy and Finance issuing policy directives.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, exporters and service providers must settle export proceeds through a licensed foreign exchange bank within the statutory due date, generally within 6 months from the date of export or service completion. If proceeds cannot be collected in that period, an extension for up to 18 months may be granted with the approval of the foreign exchange bank upon submission of justification. There is no mandatory conversion ratio; the entire export receipt may be retained in a foreign currency account. However, the exporter must report the settlement through the bank's foreign exchange database and provide export customs clearance documentation or equivalent service export evidence to the settlement bank.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability. South Korea operates a permission-based foreign exchange system; non-licensed offshore EMIs cannot legally provide multi-currency accounts or payment services to Korean entities without being registered as a foreign exchange business handler or electronic financial transaction operator under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act and Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Domestic fintechs such as Toss (Viva Republica) operate under domestic licenses, but offshore platforms like Mercury, Stripe in its EMI capacity, or similar digital lenders are only permissible for auxiliary invoicing or collection if they partner with a licensed domestic bank; they cannot serve as the primary clearing rail for FX transactions, capital escrow, or regulatory filings. Use of such EMIs as the principal treasury account would create immediate regulatory non-compliance and AML rejection.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For foreign-owned or non-resident directors, physical branch appearance is generally required for first-time account opening under the Financial Transactions Reports and Information Act. In exceptional cases, remote opening using a notarised power of attorney and certified apostilled corporate documents is permitted by certain banks, but final sign-off requires a mandatory in-branch interview with at least one statutory director or an appointed representative. For a Yuhan Hoesa LLC with all foreign directors, underwriting committees typically mandate physical presence of the representative director or a local compliance officer at a main branch for biometric verification and origin-of-funds interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital remittance from a non-bank third-party remitter not matching the beneficiary identified in the investment contract
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed and apostilled share subscription agreement or investment agreement; board resolution of the Korean entity; a notarised letter of undertaking from the actual remitting entity explaining the economic rationale; bank statement of the remitter; certified copies of the UBOs' passports; completed foreign exchange transaction report form and the bank's internal transaction-purpose cover sheet.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner or board member appears on an international or domestic sanctions watchlist or has politically exposed person status without sufficient explanation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Comprehensive sanctions and PEP screening report generated from a licensed third-party provider covering all UBOs, directors and beneficial stakeholders; an AML questionnaire addressing source of funds and source of wealth; certified copies of asset statements and title documentation; a legal opinion from a licensed Korean counsel on the applicability of any sanctions; evidence of the UBO's ordinary business operations and business consistency.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the declared business scope (DevOps/cloud tools) and the expected payment rails (Stripe_Billing, Mercury_ACH) creating a high-risk digital pattern
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan with target markets and client channels; underlying SaaS licence and subscription agreements; hosting and infrastructure contracts; proof of a functional development team such as GitHub repositories, employee list and employment contracts; a detailed payment flow chart showing how funds flow from end customers to Stripe or Mercury and into the Korean treasury account; documentation of any applicable local ICT licensing requirements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Delay or inconsistency in statutory documentary filings such as foreign investment notification, corporate registration, or tax identification during underwriting
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the foreign investment report certificate under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; corporate registration certificate or current registry extract from the Korean court; evidence of tax registration with the local tax office; an undertaking letter to provide subsequent updates within the statutory deadlines; and certified copies of the corporate bylaws and all board resolutions relating to the capital structure.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity subscriptions must be routed through a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank. The investor or the Korean entity submits a foreign exchange declaration to the designated FX bank, obtains the bank's confirmation of receipt, and causes the Korean entity to open a capital escrow account in foreign currency or KRW. The bank issues a foreign investment notification certificate after verifying the incoming wire; this certificate underpins the entity's ability to later repatriate profits. A corporate resolution authorising receipt of funds and share allocation is required. For every capital injection, the sending bank must transmit a SWIFT MT103 with the investor's full name and the appropriate Bank of Korea balance-of-payments purpose code for direct investment equity. After receipt, the Korean entity must complete the foreign investment registration within the statutory time limit and ensure that the received amount exactly matches the subscribed capital schedule.

stage_4.outbound_trade_disbursements: For cross-border payments for software licences, subscriptions, and virtual infrastructure, the Korean entity must submit the underlying contract, tax invoice, and supporting commercial documentation to the settlement bank. The bank debits the KRW account, converts to the settlement currency, and transmits via SWIFT MT103 using the appropriate service payment purpose code under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. For high-value hardware or implementation projects, an irrevocable commercial letter of credit may be issued; for recurring trade flows, documentary collections (D/P or D/A) are suitable. All outbound payments must match the beneficiary, invoice, and corporate tax identification; prior customs declarations are required if physical goods are involved. The bank will reject any disbursement lacking a legitimate underlying transaction purpose or proper supporting documentation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore KRW forward contracts for underlying trade exposure, generally with tenor up to 12 months and requiring documentary proof of export or import transactions
Foreign exchange swaps conducted through licensed Korean banks for cash-flow hedging of cross-border capital flows, subject to underlying transaction evidence and regulatory reporting
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts offered by international banks but only permitted for exceptional hedging needs with Bank of Korea approval and never for speculative purposes

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return and Local Income Tax Surcharge
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of Korea for national corporate tax; local tax authority (si/gun/gu) via the municipal Wetax system for the 10% local income tax surcharge
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 of the following fiscal year for a December 31 year-end; otherwise within 3 months after the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge of 20% of the unpaid corporate tax (40% if fraudulent), underreporting surcharge of 10% (40% if fraudulent), overdue interest on unpaid national taxes of 0.022% per day (approximately 8.03% per annum), enforced tax collection, and administrative closure of the business registration by the NTS when the entity remains dormant for more than one year; continued failure can ultimately lead to court-driven commercial registry dissolution or strike-off through the registration court.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Semi-Annual Value-Added Tax Return for the Second Half (July 1 - December 31) of the previous year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before January 25 of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional tax of 10% of the unpaid VAT for late filing (20% if fraudulent), daily overdue interest of 0.022% for late payment, and NTS administrative closure of the business registration for prolonged non-compliance or dormancy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Semi-Annual Value-Added Tax Return for the First Half (January 1 - June 30) of the current year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before July 25 of the current calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional tax of 10% of the unpaid VAT for late filing (20% if fraudulent), daily overdue interest of 0.022% for late payment, and NTS administrative closure of the business registration for prolonged non-compliance or dormancy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory External Audit Report and Audited Financial Statements (only if audit threshold is met)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) of Korea through the DART electronic disclosure system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the fiscal year-end; for a December 31 year-end, on or before March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under the Act on External Audit of Joint-Stock Companies, failure to engage an auditor or submit the audit report can result in criminal fines up to KRW 30,000,000 (approximately USD 22,000) against the company and responsible officers, administrative fines by the Financial Services Commission, mandatory supervisory designation, and the financial statements being treated as defective.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Investment Business Report (for foreign-invested Yuhan Hoesa)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before January 31 of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine generally up to KRW 2,000,000 (approximately USD 1,500) under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; failure to file may impair foreign-investment benefits and legal protection, and a separately reportable change of foreign ownership made without a change report within 30 days can trigger an additional fine and loss of investor status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Members' Meeting or Unanimous Written Resolution for Approval of Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company's general meeting of members (corporate records; no government filing is required unless the articles or applicable registration rules require registration of a resolution)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end; for a December 31 year-end, on or before March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct standalone government fee, but failure to hold the approval or to prepare valid financial statements exposes directors to civil liability, corporate governance disqualification, audit qualification, NTS dormancy closure, and administrative fines under the Commercial Act for failure to maintain required statutory records.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Registry Change Registration (annual maintenance obligation when registered matters change; no annual no-change filing is required in Korea)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registration Office of the local District Court (Korea Court Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 weeks (14 calendar days) after any change in registered matters, such as transfer of membership interest, change of members, directors, representative, registered office, or articles of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late registration penalty under the Commercial Registration Act and Commercial Act: administrative fine up to KRW 5,000,000 (approximately USD 3,800) against the company and the defaulting officer; persistent non-compliance with registry formalities may cause the court to treat the company as dormant and expose it to judicial dissolution or strike-off from the commercial register.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Joint-Stock Companies and its Enforcement Decree, an independent certified CPA audit is mandatory if any of the following applies at the fiscal year-end: (1) the company is listed or designated as a public-interest entity by the Financial Services Commission; (2) total assets exceed KRW 12,000,000,000 (approximately USD 9.2 million) as shown in the balance sheet; (3) annual turnover exceeds KRW 100,000,000,000 (approximately USD 77 million); (4) the company meets headcount and asset-based designation criteria set by the Financial Services Commission, for example more than 300 employees combined with total assets in excess of KRW 5,000,000,000 (approximately USD 3.8 million); or (5) the company is a parent or subsidiary of an audited entity required to prepare consolidated financial statements. There is no standalone headcount-only threshold for ordinary Yuhan Hoesa private entities.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for listed, public-interest, and large designated audit entities; non-listed small and medium-sized Yuhan Hoesa entities may use Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP) issued by the Korea Accounting Standards Board (KASB). The audited financial statements must clearly state the applicable framework and be prepared on a going-concern basis.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, a foreign-invested Yuhan Hoesa must file an Annual Foreign Investment Business Report with MOTIE through KOTRA by January 31 of each calendar year, confirming each foreign investor's identity, country, shareholding percentage, and the company's annual business status. Any subsequent transfer or change in the foreign investor's beneficial ownership must be reported to MOTIE/KOTRA within 30 days of the transaction. Domestically, there is no separate public UBO register filing; the Yuhan Hoesa must instead maintain an accurate Register of Members and register any change in membership, directors, or articles with the local commercial registry within 2 weeks. For AML/KYC and banking purposes, financial institutions require periodic beneficial-owner confirmation at account opening and on triggering events, and the banking UBO record must match the statutory member register.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (membership ledger of the Yuhan Hoesa, including equity interests and pledges)
Register of Directors (if one or more directors are appointed)
Register of Charges and Pledges over Membership Interests
Minute Book for Members' Meetings and Director Resolutions
Accounting Books and Financial Statements (balance sheet, income statement, tax records, and vouchers)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 900 - USD 2,800 per year for a standard registered office and Korean corporate secretarial/registered agent service for a Yuhan Hoesa
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 7,000 - USD 20,000 for a typical Korean certified audit of a non-public Yuhan Hoesa; USD 20,000 - USD 80,000 or more for large, foreign-investment-complex, or Financial Services Commission-designated audited entities

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: National CIT rate bands: 10%/20%/22%/25% plus 10% resident surtax on national CIT, producing an aggregate top marginal headline rate of 27.5%; lower aggregate effective rates are 11.0%, 22.0%, and 24.2% at the respective brackets.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D credits for DevOps infrastructure, database and API monitoring software development under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act (up to 30% of qualifying R&D costs, and up to 50% for national strategic technologies); 100% corporate income tax exemption for five years and 50% reduction for two subsequent years for qualified foreign investments in Free Economic Zones under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; job creation and facility investment tax credits may further reduce the effective rate; the compliance schema applies a five-year loss-carryforward limit.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Base and Self-Assessment Return for Foreign Corporations (including the domestic business place schedule), filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax System at www.hometax.go.kr.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The corporate income tax return must be filed within 60 days after the end of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year Korean entity the final return is due by May 31 of the following year, with non-resident branch quarterly prepayments and final adjustment integrated into the same HomeTax filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1/Line 1 - Corporate and foreign taxpayer identification
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business registration number or NTS foreign corporation registration number, corporate name, representative, head-office address and country code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the exact number shown on the NTS foreign corporation registration certificate. If the Yuhan Hoesa has no registered Korean place of business, do not apply for a separate local tax ID; Korean-source income should be reported through non-resident withholding. Non-resident shareholders must also provide their foreign tax ID on the shareholder information schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2/Line 3 - Taxable period and business-year election
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening and closing dates of the statutory accounting period and confirmation that the tax return covers a 12-month period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calendar-year filing is the default. A foreign-held Yuhan Hoesa must use the same business year as its selected GAAP accounting year, and any change requires NTS approval. Mismatched periods between the Korean return and the foreign parent's return create audit red flags in transfer pricing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3/Line 5 - Tax residence, treaty country and head office status
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of the entity's tax residence, DTA country, and whether the Korean filing is made as a resident corporation, a domestic business place of a foreign corporation, or a non-resident taxpayer with Korean-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If treaty relief is claimed on dividends, interest, royalties or service fees, attach the official Tax Residency Certificate (TRC), complete the beneficial ownership confirmation schedule, and describe the substance of the CIGA performed outside Korea. A mere nominee address or mailbox company will cause NTS to deny the reduced DTA rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4/Line 9 - Gross income and Korean-source vs foreign-source attribution
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue from DevOps tool subscriptions, database/API monitoring charges, support fees and licensing, separated into Korean-source and foreign-source streams.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If there is a dependent agent PE or a fixed place of business, report worldwide attributable revenue under the restricted force-of-attraction rule. If no PE exists, only Korean-source income is taxable, but SAAS subscription revenue from Korean end users is aggressively reviewed by NTS; the intercompany revenue split must be supported by an OECD transfer pricing study and actual contract risk allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5/Line 17 - Deductions, R&D expenses and infrastructure depreciation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Expenses properly allocable to the Korean taxable income, including software research costs, cloud infrastructure depreciation, employee compensation, intercompany service fees and interest.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions are allowed only to the extent attributable to the Korean place of business and computed on an arm's-length basis. Intercompany royalties paid to a low-tax affiliate for API code or technology support must satisfy the economic substance test, otherwise the deduction is disallowed and treated as a constructive dividend subject to 22% withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6/Line 22 - Taxable income, loss carryforward, tax credits and self-assessed tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of taxable base after adjustments, available loss carryforward, foreign tax credits, prepayment credits and the final corporate income tax plus local income tax payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Carryforward is limited to five tax years under this compliance schema. Foreign tax credits may be claimed only on taxes paid abroad on income that is also taxed in Korea and only where the relevant DTA permits. If the taxpayer claims DTA relief on outbound remittances, Box 6 must reconcile the reduced WHT applied with the actual remittances and shareholder benefit declarations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing surtax accrues at 0.05% of the unpaid national tax per day, capped at 180 days (maximum 9%); an additional 10% surcharge applies for neglected understatement, 20% for unfiled or fraudulent understatement, and 30%-40% for unfaithful reporting committed through false documents. Failure to file transfer pricing documentation separately creates a 10%-15% documentation penalty, and deliberate tax evasion can result in criminal referral with fines of up to three times the evaded tax and imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: The statutory aggregate outbound dividend withholding tax rate is 22%: 20% national withholding tax plus 2% local income tax surtax. This rate applies unless an applicable DTA reduces or eliminates the dividend withholding tax for a beneficial owner with sufficient shareholding and substance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief on outbound dividends, interest or royalties, the Korean payer and non-resident recipient must complete the following steps: (1) obtain an official Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the jurisdiction of the beneficial owner covering the year of payment; (2) file the HomeTax treaty relief application, along with the beneficial owner declaration, confirming that the recipient is not a conduit and has real economic substance; (3) submit supporting ownership certificates, board resolutions, bank statements, employment and office records, and evidence of CIGA in the residence jurisdiction; (4) the Korean remitter must apply the treaty rate before payment, or if the statutory rate was withheld, the recipient must file a refund claim with the local District Tax Office before the statutory limitation period expires; and (5) any change in shareholding, residence or substance during the year requires immediate amendment of the treaty relief registration.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory aggregate WHT on cross-border royalties and interest is also 22% (20% plus 2% local surtax). Under most Korean DTA treaties the conventional treaty cap for royalties is 15% (with 10% for certain industrial royalties) and for interest is 15%, while bank/qualified institutional interest may be exempt under a number of treaties; full documentation including TRC, beneficial ownership declaration, license contracts, and financing agreements is required to obtain the reduced rate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 50 billion of aggregate annual cross-border related-party transactions triggers mandatory Local File and Master File preparation in Korea; a multinational group with KRW 100 billion or more consolidated group revenue is subject to Country-by-Country Reporting notification and filing. NTS may also request local documentation below these thresholds during a transfer pricing audit.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not administer a formal UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations filing, but the substance-over-form principle, the general anti-abuse rule in the Framework Act for National Taxes, and the abuse-of-rights doctrine under the Adjustment of International Taxes Act apply fully. The Yuhan Hoesa must demonstrate real employees, premises, decision-making, and Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) in the jurisdictions where cloud pricing, database infrastructure contracts, intellectual property ownership, and financial risk are managed; a shell with no operational reality will lose DTA protection and Korean tax deductions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion on Korean-Source Cloud Revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Recording Korean user subscription fees for database and API monitoring services in an offshore treasury entity with no employees, while the Korean Yuhan Hoesa negotiates with Korean customers, provides support, and bears the economic risk; then omitting those receipts from the Korean corporate income tax return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 3, fraudulent evasion of corporate income tax is punishable by imprisonment for up to five years (seven years in aggravated high-value cases) and a fine of up to three times the evaded tax. NTS additionally imposes a 20% fraudulent understatement surcharge, daily late-payment interest, and may seize Korean bank accounts and receivables.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or direct the false return can be personally joint and severally liable under the secondary taxpayer provisions of the Framework Act for National Taxes if corporate assets are dissipated before collection; they face personal bank account and real estate seizure, NTS overseas travel restriction (blacklisting), and criminal imprisonment up to five years for tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure and Excessive Royalty Loading
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying a low-tax affiliate an unsupported 25% royalty for API monitoring technology and charging intercompany interest through a shareholder loan exceeding the statutory debt-to-equity threshold, while failing to prepare a transfer pricing study and failing to submit the Local File and Master File for cross-border transactions above KRW 50 billion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Adjustment of International Taxes Act Articles 4 and 13, NTS re-determines the arm's-length profit, denies interest deductions under thin capitalization, imposes transfer pricing document penalties of up to 10% of the transaction amount, and adds an understatement surcharge of 20%-40% on the resulting tax adjustment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director found to have signed the manipulated intercompany contracts, or to have actively shifted revenue to a controlled offshore corporation, can be assessed as a secondary taxpayer, lose limited liability protection where the corporation is treated as an alter ego, suffer travel blacklisting and asset freezing, and face imprisonment up to five years for evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Treaty Shopping and Beneficial Ownership Abuse in Dividend and Royalty Conduit Structures
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Inserting a newly formed zero-employee Hong Kong holding company into the dividend and royalty chain between the Korean Yuhan Hoesa and the ultimate owner solely to access a 10% DTA dividend/royalty rate and avoid the 22% Korean statutory WHT. The Hong Kong company has no office, no staff, no board minutes, and performs no CIGA with respect to licensing or dividend decisions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Framework Act for National Taxes general anti-abuse rule and the Adjustment of International Taxes Act treaty-shopping provisions, NTS denies the DTA benefits, recharacterizes the conduit as the taxable recipient, imposes the full 22% WHT, adds a 30%-40% reckless avoidance surcharge, and disallows the related intercompany royalty deductions in Korea.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors knowingly using a conduit to avoid Korean WHT are jointly and severally liable for the unwithheld tax as withholding co-obligors, may be blacklisted under the NTS travel restriction program, and can be prosecuted for aiding and abetting tax evasion, with penalties including imprisonment up to five years and fines of up to KRW 20 million.
